entries.realMaterial: Travertino Romano Classico, Tivoli-Guidonia basin east of Rome (Bagni di Tivoli quarries), sawn vein-cut (across the bed); open-pore on walls, filled (tinted cement or resin) on anything walked

workingsByEra.classical: honed (satin, no image); open voids on walls, filled on floors and treads
workingsByEra.modern: filled and polished (the Hall of Light)
workingsByEra.future: filled and polished at the Atrium's 6 m base only: the modern's last stone under the glass
workingsByEra.doorway: honed in every era: the threshold is outside time
workingsByEra.outdoors: honed, sawn or bush-hammered, then weathered (weather sets the finish)

roles: every doorway: threshold slab and surround
Salon: piers, jambs, transverse arches, voussoirs, keystones, skirting, floor under every arch, viewing stones
Nymphéas oval: floor, four curved benches, the pond's moulded coping and its carved lily frieze
Reserve: pier bases, imposts, long-stair treads
Hall of Light: floor, plinth, stereo stones
Grounds: façade, portico, parvis, kerbs, canal and basin copings, crushed-offcut gravel
entries.why: The one stone equally Classical and Modern: the Colosseum and St Peter's colonnade, and the Getty Center and Aulenti's Orsay. Warm under daylight and paintings; its voids read as stone at any distance; a living trade stone with two thousand years of outdoor record. Vein-cut bands run along the direction of travel, as a mason lays an enfilade.
entries.verdictReason: Same idea, now a named quarry and cut. The old image was procedural and the old colours (L* 86-89) lighter than any measured travertine; the stone will read darker and warmer. Classical floors are honed, not polished; one rule for open and filled voids; thresholds always honed.

research.needed: Colour of Tivoli travertine itself (only Spanish travertines measured); a tier (b) ColorChecker specimen of Travertino Romano Classico honed open, honed filled and polished; a 'crushed' working and a 'waterline' history for the Grounds.

workingsByEra.modern: absent: the anchor skips the modern

roles: Rotunda: wall ashlar, sixteen fluted pilasters, niche surrounds and sills, floor ring, dial field (two selections), lifting drum, spiral stair

entries.why: Its network of iron-and-clay stylolites is the design's crackle, found in a real stone. It is lighter than the travertine (light reflectance about 64 % against about 40 %) in the same warm hue, so the anchor glows; it is dense (0.5 % open porosity), so it takes a true mirror polish, which lets the anchor return as the future's floor; it is calcite like the travertine, so the two meet as one kind of matter.
entries.oldChoice: M_Marble_Wall (generated crackle, then ambientCG Marble014), M_SunClock_Drum, M_Elan_Mirror (#EAE2D4), M_SquareFloor
entries.verdictReason: The look is kept, the drawn crackle (read as cracked paint) retired; the procedural Marble014 is not evidence. Now also the dial's field, replacing the statuary white, so the anchor is one stone.

research.needed: a* b* of Crema Marfil; the crackle's cell size; honed and polished slip values; a mirror-polish working distinct from polished; tier (b) specimen honed and polished.

entries.realMaterial: Rojo Alicante, La Romana (Alicante): micritic limestone, iron-red with two generations of white calcite veins

entries.why: Calcite like the Crema Marfil, so it wears with it; quarried in the village next to Pinoso; the red of the dial is the red under the casts below. Ties back by physics (calcite) and by the iron-red thread.

entries.realMaterial: Pavonazzetto: violet-veined white marble from the Afyon-İscehisar district, the site of the ancient Docimium quarries (traded today as Afyon violet)

entries.why: The Romans' own pavonazzetto came from here. Ties back by hue (violet round the cream) and physics (calcite).

research.needed: Substance research record; confirm current quarry and block size for 12 shafts; a specimen of its violet veining.

entries.realMaterial: Verde antico (marmor Thessalicum): serpentine breccia from near Larissa, Thessaly, still quarried
roles: Classical Hall: floor bands and panels
entries.why: The Roman source, still worked. Ties back by hue; it is harder than the calcite fields and will stand slightly proud, as in real opus sectile.

research.needed: Substance research record and a specimen: serpentine optics and colour.

entries.realMaterial: Imperial porphyry (porfido rosso antico), Mons Porphyrites (Gebel Dokhan, Egypt): reclaimed only, sliced from ancient column stock
entries.why: The Pantheon's and every Cosmati floor's roundels are slices of ancient columns; the one stone in the museum that could only be found. Ties back by hue to the iron-red thread.

research.needed: Substance research record; owner to accept a reclaimed-only stone (open question). Reclaimed is its provenance, not a working: it is polished as any floor stone.

entries.realMaterial: Burgundy pressed brick (brique de Bourgogne), the pale buff-pink brick of Paris's cellar and reservoir vaults 1860-1900 (Montchanin works; today reclaimed or matched from a Burgundy works), in lime mortar
